title: Hypercohomology spectral sequence via a Cartan--Eilenberg resolution
statement:
Let $v$ be as in [def-sp-truncation-couple] and let $A^{\bullet,\bullet}$ be
a Cartan--Eilenberg resolution of a bounded-below complex $K^\bullet$: the
row $A^{\bullet,s}$ is an injective resolution
[def-sp-injective-resolutions] of $K^s$, and the column cohomology complexes, with the differential in the resolution
degree, are injective resolutions of $\mathcal H^s(K^\bullet)$ (the
Cartan--Eilenberg conditions of [lem-sp-cartan-eilenberg-exists], with the
indices exchanged and an arbitrary lower bound for the complex degree). Then the filtration of the total complex by the
*second* degree gives the spectral sequence

$$
 E_1^{r,s}=R^rv(K^s)\Longrightarrow
 \mathcal H^{r+s}(RvK^\bullet),
$$

$d_1:E_1^{r,s}\to E_1^{r,s+1}$, induced by the differential of $K^\bullet$
under the signed identifications $E_1^{r,s}\cong R^rv(K^s)$ (multiply the
row-cohomology identification by $(-1)^{rs}$),
and the abutment is the cohomology of the derived functor of $K^\bullet$,
independent of the resolution.

proof.text: Obtain the filtration, spectral sequence, page identifications, differentials, cycle/boundary quotients and transported total-cohomology abutment from lem-sp-cartan-eilenberg-second-filtration. Obtain the pinned augmentation and its K-injective resolution properties from lem-sp-cartan-eilenberg-total-resolution. Obtain the finite-diagonal complex comparison e from lem-sp-cartan-eilenberg-mapped-total.

For an arbitrary chosen K-injective resolution ρ, package the augmented total as a KInjectiveResolutionChoice τ. Apply clause (1) of lem-sp-kinjective-computes to τ and ρ. Choose the comparison maps u,v and the two inverse homotopies, giving a HomotopyEquiv. Apply F termwise and take its homology isomorphism. Compose with the homology of e to define c. Define w=e.hom followed by F(u). Its diagonal inclusion equation follows from the pinned equation of e, associativity and F.map_comp; its homology equation follows from HomologicalComplex.homologyMap_comp.

Instantiate the transported total-cohomology abutment from the first step at the family rightDerivedCohomologyWithResolution K ρ and the constructed c. This gives H with its finite filtration, prescribed steps and stabilized page comparisons. Combine the witnesses and compatibility equations by conjunction introduction.

statement_change.what: Column cohomology objects are not the cohomology objects of K: for a noninjective object X in degree zero, the column cohomology row is its injective resolution, not X in every resolution degree. Stacks 015H(6) says this is a resolution of H^s(K). Also Stacks 0130(4) gives (-1)^r in the second-filtration d1 under the ordinary row-cohomology identifications; signed identifications remove it, retaining the displayed unsigned differential.

old_proof.text:
Each row $A^{\bullet,s}$ is an injective resolution
[def-sp-injective-resolutions] of $K^s$, so by the definition of the right
derived functors in [def-sp-left-exact-additive] the entries $R^rv(K^s)$ are
the $r$-th cohomology of $v(A^{\bullet,s})$. Apply
[thm-sp-spectral-object-yields] to the total complex
$T^\bullet:=\operatorname{Tot}\bigl(v(A^{\bullet,\bullet})\bigr)$ with its
decreasing filtration by the second degree,
$F^sT^\bullet:=\bigoplus_{s'\geq s}v(A^{\bullet,s'})$. This is a filtration
by subcomplexes: the total differential preserves the second degree in its
first summand and raises it in its second, so $\bigoplus_{s'\geq s}$ is
stable. It is bounded in each degree $n$: $F^sT^n=T^n$ for $s$ below the
lowest nonzero degree $s_0$ of $K^\bullet$, and $F^sT^n=0$ for $s>n$ because
$A^{r,s}=0$ for $r<0$. The graded pieces are
$\operatorname{gr}^sT^\bullet=v(A^{\bullet,s})[-s]$. Item (a) of that
theorem, whose first index $p$ is the filtration index, gives with $p=s$ and
$q=r$

$$
 E_1^{s,r}=H^{s+r}\bigl(v(A^{\bullet,s})[-s]\bigr)
 =H^r\bigl(v(A^{\bullet,s})\bigr)=R^rv(K^s),
$$

and $d_1:E_1^{s,r}\to E_1^{s+1,r}$ is the boundary homomorphism of
$0\to\operatorname{gr}^{s+1}\to F^s/F^{s+2}\to\operatorname{gr}^s\to0$, which
is the map induced on $H^r$ by the vertical maps
$v(A^{\bullet,s})\to v(A^{\bullet,s+1})$; these lift the differential
$K^s\to K^{s+1}$, so $d_1=R^rv(d_K)$. The statement writes this term as
$E_1^{r,s}$, the filtration index $s$ in the second slot; it is the same
spectral sequence with the two indices listed in the other order. Item (b) of
the same theorem identifies the abutment with the cohomology of the total
complex, $\mathcal H^{r+s}(T^\bullet)$, in the sense of
[def-sp-convergence].

It remains to identify $\mathcal H^{r+s}(T^\bullet)$ with $\mathcal H^{r+s}(RvK^\bullet)$, for the
derived functor on $\operatorname{Ch}^+$ of [def-sp-kinjective-bridge]. In
total degree $n$,

$$
 \operatorname{Tot}(A^{\bullet,\bullet})^n=
 \bigoplus_{r+s=n}A^{r,s},
$$

a *finite* direct sum: the rows are resolutions, so $A^{r,s}=0$ for $r<0$, and
$K^\bullet$ is bounded below, so $A^{r,s}=0$ for $s$ below some $s_0$. A
finite direct sum of injectives is injective, so
$\operatorname{Tot}(A^{\bullet,\bullet})$ is a bounded-below complex of
injectives, hence K-injective by part (2) of [lem-sp-kinjective-computes]. The
augmentation $K^\bullet\to\operatorname{Tot}(A^{\bullet,\bullet})$ of a
Cartan--Eilenberg resolution of a bounded-below complex is a
quasi-isomorphism: its cone is, up to shift, the total complex of the
augmented double complex (the rows $K^s\to A^{\bullet,s}$), whose filtration
by the second degree is bounded as above and has acyclic graded pieces since
each augmented row is exact; so item (a) of [thm-sp-spectral-object-yields]
gives $E_1=0$, and item (b) gives that the cone is acyclic. Hence the
augmentation is a K-injective resolution of $K^\bullet$ and

$$
 RvK^\bullet\cong v\bigl(\operatorname{Tot}(A^{\bullet,\bullet})\bigr)
 =\operatorname{Tot}\bigl(v(A^{\bullet,\bullet})\bigr),
$$

the second equality because $v$ is additive
[def-sp-left-exact-additive] and the total complex is a finite direct sum in
each degree. Independence of the chosen Cartan--Eilenberg resolution is part
(1) of [lem-sp-kinjective-computes]: any two K-injective resolutions of
$K^\bullet$ give canonically isomorphic values.
